## 2026-09-06 — idearium spec-engine never loaded on a real npm install (v0.39.49)

James's own real boot log on his actual machine showed this failing
constantly: "spec-engine load failed: The requested module 'js-yaml'
does not provide an export named 'default'". Idearium's spec-engine
never loaded at all in his real environment — every idea shown in his
screenshot was stuck at 'building' forever (Repo: tesr x3, Repo:
e2e-idearium) because the thing that actually dispatches chunks
couldn't start.

Root cause confirmed by pulling the real published js-yaml@5.2.1
tarball (root package.json declares "^5.2.1") and reading its actual
dist/js-yaml.mjs: named exports only, genuinely no default export — a
real breaking change from 4.x. spec-engine/index.js's `import yaml from
'js-yaml'` was a default import, exactly why it broke. Fixed to a named
import. This session's own earlier testing never caught it — the only
js-yaml copy available in that sandbox was a borrowed 4.3.0, which
still has a default, so every prior "verified working" claim about
spec-engine was real against the wrong dependency version. Re-verified
properly this time: installed the actual 5.2.1 package for real, re-ran
the entire idearium test suite and the full 9-stage e2e pipeline test
against it — all still pass. Swept the whole codebase for the same
broken pattern elsewhere; nowhere else had it.


## 2026-09-03 — merge-regression recovery, guardian pipeline hardening, real schema separation (v0.39.48)

A merge ("Merge handoff (nexus-6, newest) into v0.39.47 base") silently
reverted the entire idearium 3.3.0 session — cli/index.js, both
userscript fixes, host.js's skipTaskbar, spec-engine's per-chunk agent
routing, all of it, back to pre-session state. Checked every affected
file individually before restoring anything (not assumed): most were
pure reverts with zero real content from the handoff side, but
api/index.js and this root package.json each had one genuinely new,
real addition from the handoff branch (a require()-is-not-defined fix,
and a new jsdom devDependency) — both kept, not lost to a blind restore.

Guardian's staleSweep forgot stale NCP clients without ever closing
their real socket — found several turns earlier this session, patched
now: the browser-side EventSource never saw an error, so its own
correct reconnect logic never fired, and a disconnected provider never
recovered. Real test, run against the pre-fix code first to confirm it
actually catches the bug, then against the fix.

Guardian can now spawn a real Clear Glass provider tab —
spawnProviderTab() + POST /providers/:id/spawn, proxying to Clear
Glass's own already-real POST /providers/:id/start. Caught and fixed a
real bug in the first draft before it shipped (passed the request-body
parser function itself instead of calling it).

.idea is now a real node/export type (lib/node-schemas/idea.js),
grounded in idearium's real IdeaCreateGate object — the missing first
link in idea -> spec compiler -> compartment/repo -> chunks -> dispatch
-> versionium. lib/node-export.js gained real tagged/queryable support
(queryDir(), AND/OR tag matching) that didn't exist at all before.

Completed the node-schemas split (all 17 types, including contract, now
each its own file — three of them, hat/component/node, had split files
sitting unused next to a duplicate inline copy before this) and found
and split the one other real schema monolith in the whole codebase,
loom/schema/definitions.js (component/seam/hook/wire/concern).

Re-ran the full idearium test suite before packaging this: 9 of 9 real
suites pass clean (70+ assertions), including the real 9-stage
end-to-end pipeline test with no mocks anywhere.



Idearium's spec-engine dispatched every chunk in a spec to one agent —
`manifest.agent`, spec-wide, `chunk.agent` was set at creation but never
actually read at dispatch time. Replaced the hardcoded 10-section
`SPEC_SECTIONS` array with `spec-engine/blocks.yaml`, a real, declared
schema where each block carries its own default agent — the routing
table James asked for. Precedence: `sectionAgents[id]` override, then an
explicit spec-wide `agent`, then the block's own default, then
`'chatgpt'`. `speceng.build` now reads `chunk.agent` per chunk, not
`manifest.agent`. Real chatgpt→gemini fallback on dispatch escalation
(`chunk-dispatch.js`), one attempt, never cascades.

Restart survival: `chunk.jobId`/`dispatchDir`/`dispatchedAt` (already
disk-backed via `saveSpec`) is the durable record — no new queue table.
`idearium/lib/guardian-stream.cjs` adds the two things that were
actually missing: `reconcileInFlightChunks()` sweeps any chunk left
`'building'` by a prior restart against guardian's real `/jobs` on boot,
and `connectGuardianStream()` subscribes live to guardian's real
`/events` SSE for `guardian.job.complete`/`.error`. Copilot's own
`_connectGuardianStream()` — the pattern this was going to copy — turned
out to build its URL from `/events` but request `/bus` instead (a
one-shot JSON endpoint, not SSE); not fixed here (separate system), not
copied into idearium either. `idearium.spec`'s long-standing false claim
that idearium handles `guardian.job.complete` is genuinely true now.

WARP primitives (`Event`/`Gate`/`Axiom`/`Stream`/`StreamLog`) can be
declared per spec, validated against `warp/core`'s real exports,
computed independently of RAID (RAID stays untouched, per instruction).

Real bugs caught by actually running the code, not by review: the
`RepoLayer` dedup check compared `rootHash` on manifests that were still
all-`pending` — every fresh spec built from the same block set has an
identical rootHash at creation, so repo-first creation would have
silently collapsed every new repo into the first one ever made. Fixed —
dedup only applies once a manifest has real completed content.
`listSpecs()`'s lightweight per-chunk projection never included
`chunk.uuid` — the new per-chunk agent `<select>` in the UI was calling
`setChunkAgent(specUuid, undefined, agent)` on every real click. `short()`
collapsed every repo's displayed id to the same string (`nexus-id-repo-`
is the constant prefix, not a distinguishing value) — added
`shortRepo()`. Brainstorms migrated off `localStorage` entirely onto a
real `idearium_brainstorms` JAA table.

Separately: all four provider userscripts
(`guardian/userscript-{chatgpt,claude,gemini,perplexity}.js`) were
building a status HUD — a real, visible "Guardian | provider vX |
ACTIVE" badge, fixed bottom-right, unconditional — directly onto the
real page. Hidden by default now (chatgpt/claude via a real settings
toggle, gemini/perplexity via `display:none`, no toggle system there).
`clear-glass/src/providers/host.js`'s automation windows get
`skipTaskbar: true` — were relying on `show:false` alone, no real
guarantee against a later `.show()` call putting one on the taskbar.

`idearium` → 3.3.0. Full detail in idearium/spec/idearium.spec and the
commit itself (`7ea8b49`).


## 2026-07-21 — RAID as universal entry point (the spine): start-point-agnostic routing

James named the actual architecture: "the request comes from co-pilot or one
of the UIs, but goes to RAID — the start point doesn't matter, as long as it
goes to RAID." RAID is the switchboard for the whole system; Cortex is the
flight recorder. Every surface funnels to RAID, RAID routes, no surface holds
a hard pointer to any fulfilling system, and every system is hot-swappable.

Built (all bus-dispatched, per James's explicit "yes" to bus over HTTP):
- cortex/core/raid/envelope.js — the universal request shape every surface
  produces. Carries a `trail` that logs every system+status+ts it passes
  through (the "input → tagged → output, every hop logged" ledger). stamp()
  is immutable — nothing lost (§0.3).
- cortex/core/raid/router.js — any surface emits raid.route.request; router
  resolves the target via the LIVE capability-registry (Phase B, hot-swappable),
  emits raid.route.decided; target fulfills → raid.route.fulfilled; surface
  hears it over SSE. No match → raid.route.no_route (honest, §1.2). RAID names
  the target, never calls it — fully decoupled. New decision path; does NOT
  touch _decide()'s existing provider selection.
- Wired live in cortex boot, fed the real capability-registry.

Verified against the REAL 217-capability registry: "gap" from copilot →
idearium, "guardian" from cli → guardian — both routed with no surface knowing
the target; nonsense → no_route. Hot-swap proven: swap the provider in the
registry, RAID routes to the new one, caller unchanged (R-002).

10 router tests + envelope tests. raid.spec → 6.3.0 (universal_router addendum).
Suite: 724 passed, 0 failed.

Follow-on (incremental, not this commit): convert each surface to route-through-
RAID one at a time, each verified, system booting throughout. The spine is in
and proven; the migration rides on top of it.


## 2026-07-20 (later) — hook registry: architect → loom migration (§10.1 ownership correction)

James: architect "got hook duty, never intended — it's supposed to build
architecture." Confirmed by evidence, not taken on faith: architect ran the
hook registry (269 hooks, full CRUD, seeding, a 30s component-registry sync
loop) while loom's boot banner had claimed "component/hook/wire/seam
registry" since v1.1.0 with ZERO hook code behind it. And Blueprint — the
actual architecture builder — received `hooks: registry` in its constructor
and never called it once (grep -c: 0). The dependency was decorative.

Migration (docs/hooks-migration.spec, written first per §3.1):
- Registry class → lib/hook-registry.js (shared, git mv, history preserved).
  Sync module likewise → lib/hook-sync-from-component-registry.js.
- LOOM is now the write authority (§10.1): owns seeding, the sync loop, and
  every /api/hooks mutation (register/update/deprecate/remove/wire/unwire).
  Since architect never dirties hooks/hook_bindings, loom's deletes can't be
  resurrected by architect's flush — same safety argument as sigma-compaction.
- ARCHITECT keeps a read-only registry view (Blueprint context + existing GET
  consumers unbroken) and answers every hook mutation with a loud 410 pointing
  to loom :3752 — redirection, not silent breakage (§1.2).
- orchestrator proxy split: /api/architect/hooks reads → architect, writes →
  loom (loom added to the SYS proxy table — it was absent; the new routes
  would have 500'd as "unknown system: loom" without this, caught before ship).
- 6 ownership-contract tests (test-hook-ownership.js): real CRUD against a real
  store + static proof of who-owns-what. The real-store test caught two of my
  own wrong fixture assumptions (hook type enum, meta.status path) — the
  registry's validation was right, my test was wrong, both times.

loom → 1.2.0. Suite: 699 passed, 0 failed.

## 2026-07-20 (later) — sigma_records compaction: the unbounded-growth item, closed

`orchestrator/lib/sigma-compaction.js` — hourly rollups + real hard-delete,
owned by sigma-writer's own process (§10.1; JaaStore's flush only protects
deletes made by the deleting process, so compaction anywhere else would race
resurrection — cortex verified to never dirty this table). Retention = the
24h short tier sigma_records was declared as in tiers.js all along (decay
never actually ran on it: its tombstone update was one of the string-where
silent no-ops fixed earlier today, and tombstones never shrank the file
anyway). Expired rows roll into `sigma_rollups` (long tier — count, avg/max
sigma, warn/halt counts, top types per hour) BEFORE deletion: compressed
history, not destroyed (§0.3). Merge-by-bucket makes a crash between
rollup-write and delete idempotent. Boot compaction + every 10min.

Verified against the real backlog, not just mocks: 13,329 rows → 8 hourly
rollups accounting for all 13,329, file 0KB on disk after flush. 8 new
tests including a real JaaStore round-trip proving deletes persist across
reload (which also caught a test-side bug: a 600ms sleep racing the store's
1500ms flush debounce — fixed by using the store's own close() contract).
Every reader confirmed to want only recent rows before setting retention
(boot.js tail-200, intelligence last-200, autonomous-loop latest-1; the
30-day macro-compiler in version.js's notes is another tree's module and
does not exist here). Suite: 693 passed, 0 failed.

  (refuses partial/corrupt extraction). Round-tripped successfully

  conversational prompt with no grammar match correctly got routed by
  RAID to an agent (`{source:'raid', agent, ...}`), but the UI only
  checked for `result.componentId` (grammar match) or non-RESOLVED
  outcomes — a RAID decision satisfied neither, was silently thrown
  away, and the function re-dispatched with `provider` hardcoded to
  `'ollama'` regardless of what RAID picked. Now uses `hr.result.agent`.
- **`nexus-repl.js`'s `snapshot` command 404'd silently, every time.**
  POSTed to `cortex/api/snapshot` (singular) — cortex only serves
  `/api/snapshots/create` (plural). Fixed the URL.
- **ChatGPT console's chunk ladder showed `RETRYING`/`ESCALATED` states
  with no way to act on them.** Wired a real `FORCE RETRY` button to
  guardian's existing `/seam/retry` — only on rungs that are actually
  the queue's current active chunk (checked the endpoint's real
  constraint first; `ESCALATED` rungs get an honest note instead of a
  button that would silently 404).
- **ChatGPT console's `PASSIVE` badge didn't reflect queue state.** Now
  shows `N QUEUED` when there's real pending work for the provider,
  distinct from idle. (Note: a deeper, earlier fix for `claimed` timing
  — `ncp.updateClient()` — already exists above this entry; this is
  complementary, not a duplicate.)

  (`:7825`) had zero generic proxy before this; verified
  `POST /gaps/:uuid/fix` is real against `service/nexus-diagnostic.js`.
- `cli/nexus-repl-descriptors.js` — `forge`, `heal`, `snapshot` now
  registered into `component-registry` (was just `forge`). `heal`'s

## v0.9.8 — 2026-06-20

### Bug Fixes

#### [CRITICAL] ChatGPT Console: badge stuck PASSIVE, SEAM chunks stall in GENERATING
**Root cause:** `client.claimed` in the NCP `_clients` map is only written via POST
`/heartbeat` (fired every 8 s). The `GUARDIAN_REGISTER` message posted immediately on
SSE connect carries `claimed: true` (after `autoClaimIfFree()` runs) but the handler
only emitted a bus event — it never wrote into the client map. So `GET /providers`
returned `claimed: false` for the first 8 s, the UI badge stayed `CONNECTED · PASSIVE`,
and any `GUARDIAN_JOB` arriving in that window was silently dropped by `handleJob()`
(`isClaimed` guard) — causing SEAM chunks to stall in GENERATING and trip watchdog retries.

**Fix:**
- `lib/ncp.js`: Added and exported `updateClient(provider, tabId, fields)` — merges
  `claimed`, `chatId`, `usage` into the live `_clients` entry without a heartbeat.
- `guardian/server.js` `GUARDIAN_REGISTER` case: Calls `ncp.updateClient()` immediately,
  so `GET /providers` reflects real claim state within the first 4 s polling cycle.

#### [HIGH] Bridge exits code 0 immediately on `npm run start:all`
**Root cause:** `package.json` `start:all` called `node bridge/server.js`, but
`bridge/server.js` is a pure factory module (`createBridgeServer()` — no self-start).
The correct entry point is `bridge/index.js`, which runs the full 7-phase boot sequence
wiring identity → registry → ledger → router → HTTP server.

**Fix:** `package.json` `start:all` and `start:core` changed from
`node bridge/server.js` → `node bridge/index.js`.

## v0.9.9 — Phase 23.7 — Gap Lifecycle: Causal Closure
**Date:** 2026-06-24
**Operator:** James Brooks (Erosmancer)

### Core changes

**lib/gap-predicate.js** (NEW)
Predicate library, dedup key, truth floor, closure verifier, TTL sweep.
Every gap carries a checkable predicate. Closure requires predicate false AND artifact exists.
Gap dedup prevents same problem spawning multiple UUIDs.

**cortex/memory/jaa-db.js**
Added: reflection_contracts, closure_attempts, gap_predicates tables (long tier).

**lib/open-loop-taxonomy.js**
createLoop() enriches every gap with predicate, artifact_requirement, dedup_key, truth_floor, ttl_ms.

**service/nexus-diagnostic.js**
Dedup check before gap insert. Gaps marked 'investigating' on dispatch.
Sweep skips investigating/resolved/expired/blocked gaps. Kills the 300-job flood.
Predicate check before re-dispatch — if predicate is false, run closure verifier.

**cortex/gap-loop.js**
Listens for guardian.job.complete (with meta.gapUuid). Runs verifyClosure after every job.
TTL sweep every 5 minutes. Registers gap-predicate in component registry.

**guardian/server.js**
createJob() writes to JAA before dispatch (§2.1). Every state transition persisted + emitted.
job.complete carries meta.gapUuid for closure verifier. Reflection contracts polling phase (every 30s).
Human-readable log lines. RAID decision captured in job meta.

**cortex/core/raid/index.js**
Public decide() exported (was missing — caused silent chatgpt fallback on every call).
Qwen async cluster classification. Learned patterns persisted to raid-clusters.json.
_clusterReviewTick: Mistral proposes new patterns when correction rate > 40%.
getState() exposes learnedPatterns count, correctionRate.

**lib/reflection.js**
Reflection contracts queued to JAA on streak threshold. verifyClosure runs each pass.
Stale queued contracts retried. getState() exposes contract stats.

**guardian/agents/co-pilot/index.js** (v1.1)
Real system operator. Reads live state (gaps, jobs, health, providers) before every response.
Qwen classifies intent. Slash prefix → RAID-gated tool execution.
Mistral generates reply with system state as context. Honest Ollama-offline fallback.
Model priority: mistral:7b-instruct-q4_K_M → qwen2.5-coder:1.5b → fallback.

**guardian/userscript-chatgpt.js**
7-selector findResponseEl. 3-minute hard timeout. Root cause of 300-job flood fixed.

**orchestrator.js**
ui/agents/ added to hotswap watcher (was missing).

**ui/agents/mistral/index.html** (NEW)
Mistral/Ollama native console. No tab bridging. Ember accent.

**ui/home/index.html**
asSend() is now a thin shell. Everything routes through co-pilot. RAID decision shown explicitly.
